name: 3.4 Contingency Tables
_note: PUSHED 2026-08-10 as aid 23301054 in the master 334437, originally at 6 questions because the bank held only five unfiled contingency-table items. EXTENDED the same day to 10 after the ten-question floor was set, by AUTHORING four new questions (q27-q30) rather than padding with material from another section. Order is now build-then-read: construct a table from a partial grid (1) and from prose alone (2), then read counts (3), separate the three denominators (4), take both conditional directions (5,6), see the addition rule as a double-count in the grid (7), recover a joint from a union (8), and finish on the Bayes chain (9). Slots 3-6, 8, 9 and the pre-FRQ keep their existing qsetids and are NOT re-filed; slots 1, 2, 4 and 7 are new. Points re-split across all ten and still total exactly 100. questions.title: Complete a Two-Way Table - fill the missing cells and margins from the counts that are given, then read one probability off the finished table
Build a Two-Way Table from a Word Problem - turn four sentences of counts into a complete 2x2 with margins, with no grid printed, then read a conditional off what you built
Read Counts off a Two-Way Table and Apply the Addition Rule - pull the joint and marginal counts from a 2x2 and combine them without double-counting the overlap
Three Denominators from One Table - compute a marginal, a joint and a conditional off the same 2x2 and name which total each one divides by
Both Conditional Directions from One Table - compute P(A given B) and P(B given A) off the same 2x2 and see that they are different numbers
Why the Two Conditional Directions Differ - work from the joint probability to both conditionals and identify which total each one divides by
Union and Neither from a Two-Way Table - count the union straight off the grid, check it against the addition rule, and find the probability of neither
Recover the Joint from the Union, then Condition - solve the addition rule backwards for P(A and B) and use it as the numerator of a conditional
Medical Test Bayes Chain - P(disease and positive), then P(positive), then P(disease given positive) from a prevalence, a sensitivity and a false-positive rate
Pre-FRQ Grade a Conditional Reading - a two-way table scenario with a grading checklist, where the student grades four sample responses against the rubric instead of writing one
